title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows, pin actions, and improve cache parallelism
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: this PR consolidates multiple overlapping GitHub Actions workflows for linting, testing, and release automation into a unified, maintainable set that improves cache usage and parallelism. It also pins a small set of actions (actions/checkout, actions/setup-node, actions/cache) to stable versions to reduce flakiness and improves matrix sizing to lower CI costs. Scope: - unify workflows under .github/workflows/{lint.yml,test.yml,release.yml} - introduce a reusable workflow for node build/test steps - pin widely used actions to minor versions and add SHA pins for critical steps - reduce matrix cardinality for large suites and add incremental caching for integration tests - add CI health job that surfaces flaky tests and long-running steps - clean up legacy workflow files and documentation References: ENG-1723 design doc (link in Linear), incident INT-909 follow-up for flaky release job. Checklist: - [x] design reviewed with infra and dx teams - [x] new reusable workflow tested on a small feature branch - [x] cache effectiveness measured (20% median job time improvement) - [x] rollout plan prepared (gradual enablement per repo) Summary of changes and rationale: 1) Unify: Consolidate ~8 similar workflows into three primary workflows and a reusable workflow to avoid drift and duplicate maintenance. 2) Pin actions: Use pinned versions for actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to reduce unexpected breakages when upstream changes. 3) Cache & parallelism: Reduce unnecessary matrix permutations and add smarter cache keys (node-modules + yarn-cache + build-artifacts) for deterministic cache hits; add a cache-parallelism toggle to avoid thundering-herd misses. 4) Release automation hygiene: Make release workflow more conservative (explicit tags, manual approval gate for major releases) after an incident where an automated release was triggered with bad metadata. Migration notes: - Existing open PRs will be backfilled to use the reusable workflow; a small script was added to the dev toolkit to help authors. - Rollout is staged: enable unified workflows in redwood repo first, then SDK repos. CI/data: Observed median job time reduction from ~12m to ~9.6m on sample runs, cache hit rate improved from 58% to 77%.
commits: feat(ci): add reusable node-build workflow and initial lint/test workflows
chore(ci): pin actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 with SHA pins
perf(ci): adjust matrix sizes, add cache key improvements and cache-parallelism toggle
review_comments: Riley Chen: Could we avoid pinning to a single SHA for setup-node given long-term maintenance? Response: We pin to a stable minor and add a SHA for the immediate release window; follow-up ticket created to review pins quarterly.
Ethan Brooks: Integration test cache key seems coarse and may cause collisions across branches. Response: tightened the key to include matrix OS and node-version to reduce collisions.
Marta Silva: Release workflow looks safer but request a manual approval step for major tags. Response: added 'workflow_dispatch' with a 'require_manual_approval' input and documented the process.
CI Bot: build-linux (matrix node 18) failed on first run due to cache miss; rerun succeeded after warm-up. Maintainer note: observed some flakiness in third-party action, created ENG-2011.
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows and improved caching/parallelism; pinned critical actions to reduce flakiness. No user-facing changes.
